arxiv-2107-07602.title: Optimal-Design Domain-Adaptation for Exposure Prediction in Two-Stage Epidemiological Studies
arxiv-2107-07602.creator: Ron Sarafian, Itai Kloog, Jonathan D. Rosenblatt
arxiv-2107-07602.description: Abstract In the first stage of a two-stage study , the researcher uses a statistical model to impute the unobserved exposures. In the second stage, imputed exposures serve as covariates in epidemiological models. Imputation error in the first stage operate as measurement errors in the second stage, and thus bias exposure effect estimates.

arxiv-2204-12033.title: Pinning control of social fairness in the Ultimatum game
arxiv-2204-12033.creator: Guozhong Zheng, Jiqiang Zhang, Zhenwei Ding, Lin Ma, Li Chen
arxiv-2204-12033.description: Abstract Decent social fairness is highly desired both for socio-economic activities and individuals, as it is one of the cornerstones of our social welfare and sustainability. How to effectively promote the level of fairness thus becomes a significant issue to be addressed.

arxiv-2309-09194.title: Exact sampling of molecules in chemical space
arxiv-2309-09194.creator: Jan Weinreich, Konstantin Karandashev, Guido Falk von Rudorff
arxiv-2309-09194.description: Abstract The concept of molecular similarity appears in many machine-learning algorithms based on the assumption that molecules with similar representations will also share similar properties. In this work, we propose a new way to study similarity measures in molecular graph space using a Monte Carlo approach.

arxiv-2508-06682.title: A version of Kapranov’s Chow quotient and smooth moduli space of point configurations in ℙ 2 {\mathbb{P}}^{2} .
arxiv-2508-06682.creator: Lev Radzivilovsky
arxiv-2508-06682.description: Abstract A new moduli space for configurations of n n ordered points in a projective plane, which is a version of Kapranov’s "Chow quotient of Grassmanians" is introduced. The new construction is a Chow quotient as well but with additional lines connecting pairs of marked points (inspired by the idea of blow up).

arxiv-2508-11260.title: unveiLing : What Makes Linguistics Olympiad Puzzles Tricky for LLMs?
arxiv-2508-11260.creator: Mukund Choudhary, KV Aditya Srivatsa, Gaurja Aeron, Antara Raaghavi Bhattacharya, Dang Khoa Dang Dinh, Ikhlasul Akmal Hanif, Daria Kotova, Ekaterina Kochmar, Monojit Choudhury
arxiv-2508-11260.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated potential in reasoning tasks, but their performance on linguistics puzzles remains consistently poor. These puzzles, often derived from Linguistics Olympiad (LO) contests, provide a minimal contamination environment to assess LLMs’ linguistic reasoning abilities across low-resource languages.

arxiv-2509-16123.title: Equitably Coloring Planar and Outerplanar Graphs
arxiv-2509-16123.creator: Daniel W. Cranston, Reem Mahmoud
arxiv-2509-16123.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Daniel W. Cranston, Reem Mahmoud. A proper s s -coloring of an n n -vertex graph is equitable if every color class has size ⌊ n / s ⌋ \lfloor n/s\rfloor or ⌈ n / s ⌉ \lceil n/s\rceil . A necessary condition to have an equitable s s -coloring is that every vertex v v appears in an independent set of size at least ⌊ n / s ⌋ \lfloor n/s\rfloor .

perkins-discourse-damned-art-english-160.title: A Discourse of the Damned Art of Witchcraft
perkins-discourse-damned-art-english-160.creator: William Perkins
perkins-discourse-damned-art-english-160.description: The great Puritan theologian's discourse on witchcraft so far as revealed in Scripture; the most influential English Reformed demonology.

plos-pone-0012505.creator: Erum Khan, Mehreen Kisat, Nabil Khan et al.
plos-pone-0012505.description: PLOS ONE research article. Demographic features of dengue fever have changed tremendously in Pakistan over the past two decades. Small scale studies from all over the country have reported different aspects of individual outbreaks during this time. However, there is scarcity of data looking at the overall

pmc-10587522.title: Evaluation of measurement accuracy of wearable devices for heart rate variability
pmc-10587522.creator: Xiangchen Li, Yuting Song, Huang Wang, Xinyu Su, Mengyao Wang, Jing Li, Zhiqiang Ren, Daidi Zhong, Zhiyong Huang
pmc-10587522.description: SummaryThis paper proposed a method based on heart rate variability (HRV) for evaluating the accuracy of wearable devices in measuring heart rate. HRV refers to the variation in time intervals between successive heartbeats, widely used in many fields such as clinical and sports fields.

pmc-11347406.title: Unveiling the therapeutic potential of Lobaria extract and its depsides/depsidones in combatting Aβ42 peptides aggregation and neurotoxicity in Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11347406.creator: Meixia Yang, Caishan Yan, Dusadee Ospondpant, Lisong Wang, Shengying Lin, Wai Lun Tang, Tina Tingxia Dong, Penger Tong, Qin Xu, Karl Wah Keung Tsim
pmc-11347406.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: The development of effective inhibitors that can inhibit amyloid β (Aβ) peptides aggregation and promote neurite outgrowth is crucial for the possible treatment of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Lobaria (Schreb.) Hoffm., a traditional Chinese medicine used in Himalaya region for inflammatory diseases, contains depsides/depsidones (DEPs) such as gyrophoric acid, norstictic acid, and stictic acid known for their anti-cancer and anti-inflammation properties. Methods: Lobaria extracts were analyzed using HPLC to identify DEPs and establish standards.

pmc-12732908.title: Ensuring the Safe Use of Bee Products: A Review of Allergic Risks and Management
pmc-12732908.creator: Eliza Matuszewska-Mach, Paulina Borysewicz, Jan Królak, Magdalena Juzwa-Sobieraj, Jan Matysiak, Nada Orsolic, Maja Jazvinšćak Jembrek
pmc-12732908.description: Honeybee products (HBPs), including honey, bee pollen, bee bread, royal jelly, propolis, beeswax, and bee brood, are increasingly used in food, nutraceutical, and cosmetic contexts. Because of their natural origin, HBPs can provoke allergic reactions ranging from localised dermatitis to life-threatening, systemic anaphylaxis.

pmc-13091543.title: Design and rationale of the SPARC trial: a phase II, single-system randomized controlled trial of immediate transfer to specialty post-arrest care
pmc-13091543.creator: Jonathan Elmer, Sara DiFiore-Sprouse, Francis X Guyette, Charity G Patterson, Steffen Ventz, Clifton W Callaway, University of Pittsburgh Post-Cardiac Arrest Service
pmc-13091543.description: BackgroundOut-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is common and often fatal. Survivors who reach the hospital require complex, time-sensitive care, but outcomes vary widely across hospitals. Observational data suggest regionalized specialty post-arrest care may improve outcomes, yet the causal effect of an early transfer strategy is uncertain and must be balanced against the risks of interfacility transfer.

pmc-13118187.title: A Retrospective Comparison of Oncologic and Staging Outcomes Between Surgical Procedures–Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery Versus Thoracotomy in Pulmonary Adenocarcinoma
pmc-13118187.creator: Bogdan Cosmin Tanase, Teodor Horvat, Alin Burlacu, Elena Chitoran, Vlad Rotaru, Traian Pătrașcu, Laurentiu Simion
pmc-13118187.description: Introduction: Lymph node status is a key prognostic factor of lung cancer. Although video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) is widely used for early-stage disease, its consistency in achieving thorough lymph node dissection remains debated. While many studies show outcomes comparable to thoracotomy, others question its reliability for accurate staging in advanced cases.

pmc-13307048.title: How NeuroArts Aid in the Well-Being of People: A Scoping Review
pmc-13307048.creator: Jon Stewart H Dy, Justine Grace E Regala, Kasandra Camelle B Tan, Bernard F Laya, Joven R Cuanang
pmc-13307048.description: NeuroArts is an emerging interdisciplinary field examining how creative and aesthetic experiences influence neural, physiological, and behavioral processes related to health and well-being. This study aimed to map and synthesize existing evidence on arts-based interventions and their impact on well-being across healthy and clinical populations. A scoping review was conducted from May to November 2025 in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines.

pmc-13370796.title: BRASH Syndrome Unmasked: Digoxin Toxicity in the Setting of Cardiogenic Shock and Multiorgan Dysfunction
pmc-13370796.creator: Spencer Boehm, Jordan Bruni
pmc-13370796.description: Digoxin, a cardiac glycoside historically used for rate control in atrial arrhythmias and symptom relief in chronic heart failure, possesses a narrow therapeutic index and is highly susceptible to pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic disruption in critically ill patients. Its use in acute decompensated heart failure and cardiogenic shock is therefore controversial.

pmc-13513461.title: Treatment-Based Recurrence of Scar Pregnancy: A Systematic Review of the Literature as a Tool for More Informed Decision-Making
pmc-13513461.creator: Stefania Carlucci, Laura Vona, Teresa Loverre, Antongiulio Capobianco, Alessandro Favilli, Guglielmo Stabile, Stefano Bettocchi
pmc-13513461.description: Objectives: Caesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) is a rare but potentially life-threatening ectopic pregnancy whose incidence has increased in recent years. Although several surgical and non-surgical treatments have been proposed, outcomes remain heterogeneous. This systematic review aimed to compare recurrence rates of CSP according to different treatment modalities and evaluate subsequent reproductive outcomes.

pmc-13539366.title: PEBP1 Regulates Ferroptosis in Acute Glaucoma: Targeted Therapy Using Engineered Exosomes
pmc-13539366.creator: Yijia Huang, Di Gong, Junhong Guo, Wei Huang, Tingyu Hu, Shengbin Tang, Li Li, Bingkai Feng, Kuanrong Dang, Simin Deng, Yong Liu, Chunyan Tan, Fei Yao, Jiantao Wang
pmc-13539366.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, primarily driven by the progressive loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) under pathological high intraocular pressure (ph‐IOP). Despite the established role of ferroptosis in RGC degeneration, specific molecular targets that can be used for clinical intervention still need to be optimized, and the slow onset of conventional gene therapy vectors is incompatible with the acute clinical course of glaucoma.

pmc-13569275.title: Effects of elevated CO 2 and temperature on cocklebur ( X anthium strumarium L.) and its herbicide response
pmc-13569275.creator: Islam Emrah Suer, Nihat Tursun
pmc-13569275.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundClimate change, characterized by rising atmospheric CO2 and temperature fluctuations, significantly alters crop‐weed interactions and weed management efficacy. pmc-13590572.title: The venezuelan scientific diaspora as a transnational actor: knowledge circulation, STI cooperation, and development
pmc-13590572.creator: Luisa F. Echeverría-King, Branislav Pantović, Kleinsy Bonilla, Daniela Moreno Garcia, Estiven González-Sarmiento
pmc-13590572.description: This study examines the potential of the Venezuelan scientific diaspora to contribute to the development and strengthening of scientific and technological ecosystems in their countries and regions of residence. This study examines the engagement capacities, interests, collaborative practices, and perceived barriers of the Venezuelan scientific diaspora residing across different world regions.

pmc-13674823.title: Effectiveness of immersive virtual reality‐based interventions for alleviating peri‐ and post‐procedural pain and anxiety in gynecologic settings: A systematic review and meta‐analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-13674823.creator: Cristina González‐Lara, Marina Piñar‐Lara, Esteban Obrero‐Gaitán, Héctor García‐López, Irene Cortés‐Pérez
pmc-13674823.description: BackgroundNon‐pharmacological and complementary therapeutic, notably immersive virtual reality‐based interventions (IVR), could alleviate pain and anxiety associated with gynecologic procedures.ObjectiveTo evaluate the effectiveness of IVR in reducing peri‐ and post‐procedural pain and anxiety in gynecologic procedures. Secondarily, to determine the safety of IVR.
